beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string only from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit it to source control or write it to logs; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Create a single long-lived MongoDB/DocumentDB client instance (connection pool) at app startup and reuse it across requests rather than opening a new connection per request.
Ensure TLS/SSL is enforced in the connection string (e.g., tls=true / ssl=true) and validate server certificates rather than disabling certificate verification.

Prefer least-privilege credentials: create and use a database user with only the specific roles required (e.g., readWrite on sample_retail_01) rather than using an account-level master key in the app.
Avoid embedding secrets (OpenAI API key, DB creds) in code or config files; read them from environment/runtime secret store and log only non-sensitive diagnostic info.
Encode and store embeddings consistently (e.g., float32 vector) in a dedicated field (embedding) and validate dimension and dtype on insert so all documents use the same vector length and format.

When storing embeddings as BSON Binary, choose a single Binary subtype and explicit endianness and include metadata (e.g., dtype='float32', dims=1536) in the document so clients/indexes decode vectors correctly.
Normalize vectors at write time if you plan to use cosine similarity (store unit vectors) and ensure the index/query metric matches that normalization (cosine vs L2).

Before attempting to create server-side vector indexes, query the server capabilities (buildInfo or isMaster/hello) and verify the cluster supports the specific vector index plugin (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN) and the exact createIndex syntax the driver will send.

If server-side vector index creation is unsupported or fails, fall back to a client-side two-step approach: retrieve a candidate set (e.g., approximate or metadata filter) and perform exact float32 similarity ranking in application code.

When creating a server-side vector index specify index parameters explicitly (dimension, metric: 'cosine' or 'l2', index_type: 'ivf'/'hnsw', nlist/nprobe or efConstruction/efSearch) according to the server's supported options.
Keep vector dimensions fixed and reject/normalize any document whose embedding length differs from the collection's configured dimension to avoid index/query errors and inconsistent results.

Use top-k retrieval followed by exact re-ranking: request a slightly larger candidate set from the vector index (e.g., top 50) and then compute exact distances on the stored float vectors to return the final top 10.
Implement exponential backoff and limited retries for transient network and server errors, and avoid retrying non-idempotent writes without application-level protections.
Use bulk/batched writes for seeding large datasets (insert_many with ordered=False or driver bulk API) to improve throughput and handle duplicate-key or transient errors in the batch.

Provision collection throughput (RUs or shard/compute sizing) with headroom for index builds and vector search; prefer autoscale or temporarily higher throughput during heavy seeding/indexing operations.
Do not shard or select a shard key based on the embedding field; choose a high-cardinality scalar field (customer_id, product_id) for shard keys if sharding is required.
When returning search results, project only the needed fields (omit the full embedding binary) to reduce network transfer and exposure of binary vectors in API responses.
Rate-limit and possibly cache /embed and /search requests server-side to control OpenAI API costs and limit DocumentDB query load; cache popular query embeddings and results for a short TTL.

Validate and sanitize any user-supplied query fields and do not construct database commands by concatenating user input—use parameterized queries and the driver's query objects to avoid injection (e.g., malicious $where or aggregation stages).

Monitor and log index build attempts and failures; if a server reports 'unknown plugin' or similar, record the full error and fall back to client-side ranking or a different index strategy rather than retrying the same failing operation.
Enable and use driver-level options like retryWrites/retryReads and appropriate socket/heartbeat timeouts if supported by the server to improve resilience to transient faults.
Keep embedding dtype as float32 (not float64) to reduce storage and memory footprint and ensure vector index implementations which expect 32-bit floats behave as intended.
Use server-side aggregation pipelines to filter candidate documents by metadata (category, price range) before running vector retrieval to reduce work and improve precision and cost-effectiveness.
Treat index creation as an administrative operation: perform it from scripts/tools with elevated privileges during maintenance windows, not from an unauthenticated web request path.
